surprises: D7 ICON CALL, resolved on evidence rather than the fallback: slide 9's five icons are native SVG carried on the asvg:svgBlip extension, so python-pptx's shape.image raises 'no embedded image' for them -- an instrument-domain miss, not an absent asset. Resolving the relationship layer produced five distinct SVGs (1674-3843 bytes, image26-30.svg), so the FIVE DISTINCT ICONS branch applies and the sanctioned gear fallback was NOT needed. Had I stopped at the first error I would have shipped the fallback for a reason that was not true.

MY OWN ICON-ORDERING BUG, caught by a denominator: the first extraction matched each icon to its nearest pillar title by centre-to-top-left distance. It collided -- two icons claimed one pillar, two claimed another, two pillars got none -- and because the filename came from the match it silently OVERWROTE, producing 3 files for 5 icons. A clean '5 of 5 icons found' on the FIND step said nothing about the ASSIGN step. Redone by x-position (the strip is a five-across row) with slide 9's own 01..05 number boxes as an independent control, which agreed.

COUPLING NOT NAMED BY THE PRD, PRIMER, OR TO: src/lib/firmAccess.ts carries a per-firm route allowlist that is DENY-BY-DEFAULT, and its header requires values to match the <Route path> exactly. Renaming /cma -> /philosophy without updating it would have made the Philosophy page unreachable for ALL FOUR partner firms (49financial, inflection, cottonwood, demo), each silently bounced to /market. Found by asking what REFERENCES the route rather than working the spec's file list. Updated in all four.

'SAME COMMIT' IS STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE FOR C7 AS WRITTEN: the route rename lands in the portal SUBMODULE and CLAUDE.md lives in the workspace repo. Two repositories cannot share a commit, so even a BASE_EXEC seat could not have satisfied the literal same-commit condition here. The TO's same-turn escape is the only reachable branch. Worth fixing in the TO template for the next cross-repo doc-condition.

The TO's suggested Rule 25 replacement text is phrased as though it substitutes the parenthetical INSIDE Andrew's verbatim quote. Applied literally there it would rewrite his words. Flagging so the next seat to touch this does not do that.

SAME GATE CONFLICT AS THE TO-1 INSTANCE, and it GENERALIZES -- 4 artifact-coverage violations here vs 2 there, from one cause. proof-of-spec-check's coverage heuristic scans criterion_id ONLY (:53,:62) and wants the artifact stem inside the id per its {firm}-{group}-{artifact}-{check} grammar, while this TO pins the id set to C1..C8 and the same script rejects any id outside that set. Unresolvable without a false declared_exclusion or a mis-typed artifact kind; neither done. Every other rule in the checker passes. Two instances now fail the same way for the same reason, so this is a template-level incompatibility between the TO grammar and the checker, not a per-instance authoring slip. Routed to COO/CVO.
